headline: Wisconsin's Clean Energy Surge: 7,300+ MW Solar, 54M Trees
meta_description: Wisconsin has approved over 7,300 MW of solar since 2019 and planted 54 million trees since 2021, with CO2 levels now 45% below 2005.
summary_short: Wisconsin utilities have cut carbon emissions nearly in half since 2005, backed by massive solar expansion and tree-planting initiatives.
body:
Wisconsin utilities have identified CO2 levels 45% below 2005 levels in 2024, marking a significant milestone in the state's shift toward clean energy.

The progress reflects years of deliberate action. Since 2019, Wisconsin has approved more than 7,300 megawatts of solar capacity—enough to power hundreds of thousands of homes. Alongside that renewable boom, the state has planted over 54 million trees since 2021, a natural investment in both carbon sequestration and long-term environmental health.

These efforts extend to households too. Wisconsin has distributed more than $15 million in home energy rebates, helping residents upgrade to efficient systems and reduce their energy consumption. Together, these three initiatives—utility-scale solar, reforestation, and household efficiency—paint a picture of coordinated environmental progress across sectors and scales.
quick_facts: $15M+ in home energy rebates paid out
